## Source: amazon-inspector (8a271155be7da40cba43376d6a085b75a96c0bb9fed885c421424bc42fd8d07b)
setup.py defines custom build_py and install cmdclasses that, on sdist build and install, POST a JSON payload containing the installer's hostname, current working directory, install path, Python version, and a timestamp to the hardcoded bare-IP URL http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The destination is a bare IPv4 address on a non-standard port with no TLS and no relation to any declared publisher domain. A source-code comment labels the behavior an 'authorized dependency-confusion canary', but the package is published on public PyPI where any installer who resolves this name will transmit their host identifiers to that endpoint. The sdist is the only distribution file and auto-executes on default pip install for every listed platform.

## Source: kam193 (253796cb8693d039c09267f3d6d398031e3ad27640bb70f21f2e75d2578be649)
Installing the package or importing the module exfiltrates basic information about the host, and the package has no other purpose.

 - The package overrides the install command in setup.py to execute malicious code during installation.
